card.name: Small words before risk statements
card.fires_on: Short linking words (an, to, the, be) and mid-word pieces such as 'iate' in 'potentiate', just before a stated risk, rate or effect. Seen in label text on clotting risk and bleeding risk.

modes.label: Linking word before risk
modes.description: A short word like an, to, be or the right before an increased-risk or rate statement.
modes.example: Some of these studies indicate<< an>> approximate two-fold increased risk.

modes.label: Inside split-up words
modes.description: Partway through a drug or science word that is split into pieces, such as theophylline or potentiate.
modes.example: concurrent use of an NSAID or aspirin may potent<<iate>> this risk of bleeding.

card.writes: It suppresses words like worse, worst and avoidance, and promotes positive Chinese words, so it adds no clear risk wording.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words just before a label says how much a risk is raised.
